what_its_for: Cefiderocol is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections in your urinary tract, lungs (hospital-acquired pneumonia), or bloodstream caused by certain hard-to-treat bacteria. It is often used when other antibiotics have not worked or cannot be used.
how_to_take: Cefiderocol is given through an IV (intravenous) line directly into your vein by a nurse or doctor in a hospital or clinic setting. You will NOT take this medicine by mouth at home. Each infusion is slowly given over 3 hours. Make sure to tell your nurse if you feel any pain, burning, or swelling at the IV site during the infusion.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, kidney function, and the type of infection you have. The typical adult dose is 2 grams given every 8 hours (three times a day), each infused over 3 hours. Your dose may be adjusted if your kidneys are not working normally. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a medical setting, a missed dose is unlikely. However, if you miss or are late for a scheduled infusion appointment, contact your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not try to double up on doses.
storage: Cefiderocol will be stored and prepared by your healthcare team. If you are somehow given vials to take to another facility, keep them refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C) and protect them from light. Do not freeze. Once the medicine is mixed and ready to infuse, it should be used within the time frame specified by the pharmacist.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting cefiderocol. Avoid starting any new medications without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first. Do not stop your antibiotic treatment early, even if you start feeling better — finishing the full course is important to clear the infection completely.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness); severe or watery diarrhea (which may be a sign of a dangerous bowel infection called C. difficile); seizures; confusion or unusual changes in mood or behavior; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or any new or worsening symptoms during your treatment.
when_it_works: Some patients start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment, but it is important to complete the entire course of antibiotics your doctor prescribes, even if you feel well. Stopping early can allow the bacteria to come back and become harder to treat. Your doctor will monitor your progress with lab tests and check-ins.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your dose will likely be adjusted if your kidneys are not working well. Your healthcare team will monitor your kidney function during treatment. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits will be carefully discussed with you. Elderly patients: Older adults may need dose adjustments based on kidney function and will be monitored closely. Children: The safety and effectiveness of cefiderocol in children under 18 years old has not been fully established. Use in children will be based on your doctor's judgment.
